A capacitor (originally known as a condenser) is a passive two-terminal electrical component used to store energyelectrostatically in an electric field. The forms of practical capacitors vary widely, but all contain at least two electrical conductors (plates) separated by a dielectric (i.e. insulator). The conductors can be thin films, foils or sintered beads of metal or conductive electrolyte, etc. The “nonconducting” dielectric acts to increase the capacitor’s charge capacity. A dielectric can be glass, ceramic, plastic film, air, vacuum, paper, mica, oxide layer etc. Capacitors are widely used as parts of electrical circuits in many common electrical devices. Unlike a resistor, an ideal capacitor does not dissipate energy. Instead, a capacitor stores energy in the form of an electrostatic field between its plates.

When there is a potential difference across the conductors (e.g., when a capacitor is attached across a battery), an electric field develops across the dielectric, causing positive charge +Q to collect on one plate and negative charge −Q to collect on the other plate. If a battery has been attached to a capacitor for a sufficient amount of time, no current can flow through the capacitor. However, if a time-varying voltage is applied across the leads of the capacitor, a displacement current can flow.

An ideal capacitor is characterized by a single constant value for its capacitance. Capacitance is expressed as the ratio of the electric charge Q on each conductor to the potential difference V between them. The SI unit of capacitance is the farad (F), which is equal to one coulomb per volt (1 C/V). Typical capacitance values range from about 1 pF (10−12 F) to about 1 mF (10−3 F).

The capacitance is greater when there is a narrower separation between conductors and when the conductors have a larger surface area. In practice, the dielectric between the plates passes a small amount of leakage current and also has an electric field strength limit, known as the breakdown voltage. The conductors and leads introduce an undesired inductance and resistance.

Capacitors are widely used in electronic circuits for blocking direct current while allowing alternating current to pass. In analog filter networks, they smooth the output of power supplies. In resonant circuits they tune radios to particular frequencies. Inelectric power transmission systems, they stabilize voltage and power flow.

blocks.text: Dual RJ45 Ethernet Connector Breakout Board with Pin Header

This Dual RJ45 Ethernet Connector Breakout Board is designed to simplify the integration of two standard RJ45 ports into custom electronic or networking assemblies. The board presents each RJ45 jack mounted on a small PCB, with the signal lines broken out to a dual-row 0.1″ pin header as well as optional solder pads, facilitating connection to microcontrollers, switches, or other circuitry. The pair of RJ45 jacks sit side by side, enabling two separate network lines to be brought onto a single module.

When a network cable is plugged into either RJ45 jack, the signals (e.g. the eight conductors plus shield) are routed through internal PCB traces to the corresponding header pins. These header pins allow the board to interface with other modules, breadboards, or connectors without directly mounting the heavy RJ45 jacks there. The board serves as a mechanical and electrical intermediary, providing strain relief, stable mounting, and clear signal routing.

Used during prototyping, test setups, or compact network expansions, this breakout board allows designers to integrate dual Ethernet ports without fabricating custom PCBs. Its layout usually includes ground planes or shielding paths, and the board may also include LED indicator footprints or integrated resistor networks. The lightweight and modular nature of the board makes it easy to swap into existing designs, extend functionality, or debug individual network links without significant rework.

blocks.text: SPDT Micro Limit Switch Long Roller Lever 28mm 16A

The SPDT Micro Limit Switch Long Roller Lever 28mm 16A is a compact electromechanical switching device designed to detect motion, position, or mechanical limits within equipment and automation systems. It operates through a small internal snap-action mechanism that changes the contact state when the lever is pressed by a moving object or component. Because it uses a Single Pole Double Throw (SPDT) configuration, the switch can alternate between two circuit paths, allowing flexible control and signal switching in different electrical systems. This type of switch is commonly installed where reliable mechanical feedback is needed.

The long roller lever, typically around 28mm in length, improves the sensitivity and reach of the switch compared with standard push-type micro switches. The roller at the end of the lever reduces friction and allows smoother actuation when contacted by sliding or moving parts. This design helps ensure consistent triggering and reduces wear during repeated operation cycles. Due to its precise snap-action behavior, the switch can respond quickly when a mechanical movement reaches a defined position or limit.

blocks.text: ADS1115 16-Bit ADC- 4 Channel with Programmable Gain Amplifier

ADS1115 16-Bit ADC – 4 Channel with Programmable Gain Amplifier is mostly used for microcontrollers project which needs an analog-to-digital converter or when you want a higher-precision ADC. ADS1115 16-Bit ADC- provides 16-bit precision at 860 samples/second over I2C. The chip can be configured as 4 single-end input channels or two differential channels.

Additionally, ADC also includes a programmable gain amplifier, up to x16, to help boost up smaller single/differential signals to the full range. We like this ADC because it can run from 2V to 5V power/logic, can measure a large range of signals and it’s super easy to use. It is a great general-purpose 16-bit converter.

The ADS1115 chip is fairly small so it comes on a breakout board with ferrites to keep the AVDD and AGND quiet. Interfacing is done via I2C. The address can be changed to one of four options (see the datasheet table 5) so you can have up to 4 ADS1115’s connect on a single 2-wire I2C bus for 16 single end inputs.

To get you start, we have example code for both the Raspberry Pi (in our Adafruit Pi Python library) and Arduino (in our ADS1X15 Arduino library repository) Simply connect GND to ground, VDD to your logic power supply, and SCL/SDA to your microcontroller’s I2C port and run the example code to start reading data.

The use of pulse width modulation (PWM) mode to achieve the benefits of dimming / speed control is energy supply can be fully utilized, the high efficiency of the circuit. For example: When the output is 50% of the square wave pulse width modulation (PWM) power supply circuit of energy consumption for 50%, or almost all of the energy is converted to an output load power. And when using a common resistance buck governor, to make available to the load Maximum output power of 50%, the power supply must provide 71% power output, 21% of which is consumed in the resistor voltage drop and heat consumption.

2. using pulse width modulation (PWM) mode allows the load to get the full supply voltage is at work, which will help to overcome the inherent motor winding resistance leaving the motor generates a greater torque.

makers-1438.summary: NE555 Timer IC DIP-8 is a precision timer used for delays, pulse generation, and oscillation in circuits, ideal for timing and waveform applications.

blocks.text: The NE555 Timer IC in the DIP-8 package is one of the most iconic and widely used integrated circuits in the field of electronics. Designed as a highly stable and versatile timer, it is capable of producing accurate time delays or oscillations in a wide range of applications. Its internal architecture includes two comparators, a flip-flop, an output stage, and a discharge transistor, all working together to control timing intervals with precision. The device operates in two primary modes monostable and astable making it suitable for both pulse generation and continuous oscillation.

In monostable mode, the NE555 acts as a one-shot pulse generator, where the output goes high for a fixed duration determined by an external resistor and capacitor. In astable mode, it functions as a free-running oscillator, generating a continuous square wave whose frequency and duty cycle are set by two external resistors and one capacitor. The device is known for its ability to operate over a wide voltage range, typically from 4.5V to 15V, and its output can source or sink up to 200mA, allowing it to drive loads such as relays, LEDs, and small motors.

The NE555’s simplicity, reliability, and low cost have made it a favorite among hobbyists, students, and professional engineers for decades. Its ability to be configured in numerous ways from timers and PWM controllers to frequency dividers and pulse detectors underscores its flexibility. Encased in an 8-pin dual in-line package, the NE555 remains a fundamental component in both educational projects and industrial systems, embodying a perfect balance of performance and accessibility.

blocks.text: The 7476 is a dual master-slave J-K flip-flop integrated circuit in a 16-pin DIP package. Each of the two flip-flops features separate J and K inputs, a clock input, and asynchronous preset and clear inputs, allowing independent control and initialization. On the rising (or falling, depending on the variant) edge of the clock, the master captures the J/K inputs, while the slave outputs are then updated, preventing race conditions. The outputs include both Q and Q̅ (not-Q), providing complementary signals. Thanks to its master-slave architecture, the 7476 avoids the unstable “race” behavior seen in simpler J-K circuits. This makes it suitable for use in counters, registers, sequential logic circuits, and digital control systems where edge-triggered, bistable storage is needed.

makers-493215.summary: IRF540NPBF is a robust 100V, 33A N-Channel HEXFET MOSFET in a TO-220 package. Features very low 44mΩ on-resistance, fast switching, and is avalanche rated.

blocks.text: The IRF540NPBF is a member of International Rectifier’s advanced HEXFET® family of N-channel power MOSFETs. Its design leverages sophisticated stripe planar processing techniques engineered to maximize silicon efficiency, achieving an exceptionally low channel resistance. This fundamental architectural advantage is the key to its performance, minimizing the inherent losses during conduction. The device is housed in the ubiquitous TO-220AB package, a industry-standard choice that offers an excellent balance of cost-effectiveness and thermal performance for commercial and industrial power levels.

This MOSFET is built not just for efficiency but also for durability in demanding electrical environments. It is characterized by a very fast switching speed, which is crucial for modern high-frequency power conversion circuits, reducing switching losses. Furthermore, the device is fully rated for repetitive avalanche energy, meaning it can safely withstand voltage spikes and inductive load transients that would destroy less robust components. This ruggedness, combined with a high maximum operating junction temperature of 175°C, ensures reliable operation under stressful conditions.

The combination of ultra-low on-resistance, fast switching, and rugged avalanche capability makes the IRF540NPBF a highly efficient and reliable building block for power electronics. It serves as a versatile and trusted workhorse component, allowing designers to create simpler, more efficient, and more robust circuits. Its design prioritizes both performance in operation and resilience against real-world electrical stresses, solidifying its role as a fundamental solution for managing significant power levels.

blocks.text: The ceramic capacitor marked “153” (15 nF) represents a mid-value monolithic ceramic device designed for general signal, decoupling and filtering tasks. By providing a 15 nF nominal capacitance, it bridges the gap between small-value bypass capacitors and larger bulk capacitors, making it a versatile choice in board-level design. This component is non-polarized and can be reliably inserted in either orientation, allowing flexible layout choices in both through-hole and radial-lead formats.

Its typical rated voltage (50 V in one variant) ensures compatibility with a broad range of low-voltage power rails and analogue circuits. Constructed using a class-II (X7R) dielectric in some instances, the capacitor offers compact size while maintaining adequate stability over a standard operating temperature range. The leads or terminals are spaced appropriately for PCB insertion or perf-board mounting, making it suitable for both prototyping and production.

In the design phase, the 15 nF capacitor offers a balance of capacitance and footprint, making it a candidate for coupling AC signals between stages, or smoothing moderate power-supply ripple without occupying the space of a bulk electrolytic. While its performance will vary with temperature, voltage and frequency (as is typical for class-II ceramics), the device remains a dependable, low-cost passive component in many electronic systems. Its availability in standard sizes and quantities makes it convenient for sourcing and assembly.

makers-483579.summary: Parameter Value Manufacturer: MICROCHIP Mfr. Part: AT89C2051-24SU Package: SOIC-20-300mil Description: 51 Series SOIC-20-300mil Microcontrollers

blocks.text: AT89C2051-24SU 2KB 4V~6V 51Series 128Byte 24MHz FLASH 15 SOIC-20-300mil Microcontrollers (MCU/MPU/SOC) SMD IC

The AT89C2051-24SU is a low-voltage, high-performance CMOS 8-bit microcontroller from Atmel’s 8051 family. It is built around a versatile 8-bit CPU that is fully compatible with the industry-standard MCS-51 instruction set, making it easy to program using a vast ecosystem of existing tools and code. The heart of the device is its 2KB of on-chip Flash programmable and erasable read-only memory (PEROM), which provides non-volatile storage for the application code and can be rewritten up to 10,000 times. This is complemented by 128 bytes of internal RAM for data manipulation during program execution.

This microcontroller is a highly integrated system-on-chip. It packs a significant number of on-chip peripherals to minimize external component count, including two 16-bit timer/counters, a full-duplex UART for serial communication, and a precision analog comparator. It offers 15 programmable I/O lines, with ports capable of directly driving LEDs. The inclusion of a six-interrupt source, two-level interrupt architecture allows it to respond promptly to external and internal events, which is crucial for real-time control applications.

The device is designed for a wide 4V to 6V operating range and can achieve a top clock frequency of 24 MHz, providing the necessary processing speed for many embedded tasks. It features fully static operation, allowing the clock to be slowed down to zero for ultra-low power consumption. To further conserve energy, it supports two software-selectable power-saving modes: Idle Mode, which halts the CPU while keeping peripherals active, and Power-down Mode, which freezes the oscillator, reducing power to a minimal level until the next hardware reset. It is housed in a compact SOIC-20 surface-mount package.
Fully Static Operation: 0 Hz to 24 MHz.

High-precision GY-63 MS5611-01BA03 Barometer Pressure Sensor Module provides accurate digital pressure and temperature measurements for altimetry and weather monitoring. This compact board integrates the MS5611-01BA03 high-resolution MEMS sensor with a 24-bit ΣΔ ADC, delivering up to 10 cm altitude resolution over a 10–1200 mbar range. It includes a built-in voltage regulator and level shifters, so the module accepts a 3.3–5 V supply and I²C/SPI logic. The MS5611 sensor is factory-calibrated for linear pressure response, yielding precise pressure and temperature data with selectable conversion modes to balance speed and power consumption. VCC is the power pin. You can connect it to 5V output from your Arduino.
GND is the common ground for power and logic.
SCL is the SPI Clock pin, its an input to the chip.
SDA is the Serial Data In (MOSI) pin, for data sent from your microcontroller to the MS5611.
CSB is the Chip Select pin. If you want to connect multiple MS5611’s to one microcontroller, have them share the SDA, SDO and SCL pins and assign each one a unique CSB pin.
SDO is the Serial Data Out (MISO) pin, for data sent from the MS5611 to your microcontroller.
PS is Protocol Select pin. Pull it LOW to enable an SPI communication.
SCL is also the I2C clock pin, connect to your microcontrollers I2C clock line.
SDA is also the I2C data pin, connect to your microcontrollers I2C data line.

CSB pin determines the I2C address of the module. When you leave the CSB pin unconnected, the default I2C address is 0x77Hex and when you connect it to VCC, the line is pulled HIGH and the I2C address becomes 0x76Hex.
PS is Protocol Select pin. Leave it unconnected to enable an I2C communication.

blocks.text: UNI-T UT3550 Hand Held Battery Tester

The UNI-T UT3550 is a portable battery internal-resistance tester designed for real-time, on-the-spot evaluation of battery condition. It presents itself as a handheld instrument with a clear, operator-focused interface that guides users through measurement steps, zeroing and result storage. The unit is intended to simplify routine battery checks by giving immediate, easy-to-read feedback so technicians can quickly decide on battery status without lengthy setup.

Operation centers on a four-terminal measurement flow: connect the supplied leads, perform a short-circuit zeroing step to remove lead offsets, and trigger the measurement. The instrument’s menus and onscreen prompts walk users through calibration, measurement mode selection and saving results; data can be captured locally for later review. Its design balances handheld portability with workflow features found in benchtop testers, aiming to reduce measurement errors and speed inspection cycles.

The UT3550 emphasizes practical usability for field and production environments: it supports automated data recording, simple comparator-based sorting (pass/fail), and connectivity for remote control and data transfer. In short, it’s a focused tool for technicians and engineers who need reliable, repeatable battery checks with quick access to saved test records.

It’s part of the 1.5KE series, rated for a 1500 watt peak pulse power capability (1 ms pulse) and constructed in a molded plastic case with a polarity band marking the cathode. The device is intended as a surge protection element that clamps harmful voltage spikes and redirects surge energy away from sensitive components.

The device is specified to have a nominal working standoff (VRWM) of 171 V and a controlled breakdown range (VBR) near 190–210 V (measured at the specified test current). Under the standardized 10×1000 µs surge waveform the part’s clamping voltage and pulse current characteristics are given so designers can predict the maximum voltage seen by protected circuitry during a surge. Thermal and soldering limits are stated to ensure reliable mounting and operation.

The datasheet emphasises fast response, low dynamic impedance and excellent clamping capability. It calls out high-temperature soldering capability (260°C, 10 s) and a wide operating temperature range (-55°C to +175°C), highlighting the part’s suitability where both electrical robustness and mechanical/thermal reliability are needed. Mechanical dimensions and lead length recommendations (0.375″, 9.5 mm) are provided for proper PCB mounting and heat-sinking practices.

makers-470104.summary: Intel’s P8039AHL is an HMOS II 8-bit ROMless microcontroller with 128B RAM, 27 I/O lines, and a timer. Targets embedded control with external memory flexibility

blocks.text: The P8039AHL is an HMOS II-based microcontroller from Intel’s MCS®-48 family, designed as a self-sufficient, single-chip 8-bit parallel computer. It integrates a CPU, RAM, timer/counter, and I/O control on a single silicon die, leveraging Intel’s advanced N-channel silicon gate process. Unlike ROM-embedded variants, it omits internal program memory, relying solely on external storage for flexibility in system design.

Optimized for real-time control and arithmetic processing, the P8039AHL executes instructions rapidly (1.36 µs cycle time) using a lean instruction set dominated by single-byte operations. It supports binary and BCD arithmetic, bit manipulation, and two interrupt channels, prioritizing efficiency in embedded environments. The absence of on-chip ROM simplifies prototyping, allowing developers to tailor external memory to application needs.

Engineered for expandability, the microcontroller interfaces with MCS®-80/85 peripherals and external RAM/ROM via a bidirectional bus. Its on-board oscillator minimizes external components, while quasi-bidirectional I/O ports (27 total lines) streamline peripheral connectivity. The design emphasizes low-power operation, featuring RAM standby mode for data retention during voltage drops.
HMOS II Technology: High-performance, single 5V operation.
Expandable Memory/I/O: Supports external RAM/ROM and MCS®-80/85 peripherals.
On-Chip Timer: 8-bit timer/event counter for scheduling.
Dual Interrupts: Two single-level, maskable interrupts.

تُعد العدسة المكبرة اليدوية تي اتش 600558 من الأدوات المفيدة جدًا لكل من يحتاج إلى رؤية أوضح للتفاصيل الصغيرة أثناء القراءة أو الفحص أو العمل اليدوي الدقيق. فهي تجمع بين العدسة المكبرة والإضاءة المدمجة في تصميم واحد عملي وسهل الاستخدام، مما يجعلها مناسبة للاستخدام المنزلي والمهني والتعليمي في نفس الوقت.

توفر هذه العدسة تكبيرًا بمعدل 4 مرات تقريبًا، وهو ما يساعد على رؤية الكتابة الصغيرة، والتفاصيل الدقيقة، والعلامات المطبوعة، وأرقام المكونات، والملصقات، والتعليمات، والخرائط، والطوابع، والعملات، وغيرها من الأشياء التي يصعب رؤيتها بوضوح بالعين المجردة. لذلك فهي مناسبة جدًا للأشخاص الذين يحتاجون إلى رؤية أدق أثناء القراءة أو الفحص أو الصيانة.

كما تحتوي العدسة على 6 وحدات إضاءة ليد مدمجة تساعد على تحسين الرؤية في الأماكن ذات الإضاءة الضعيفة أو أثناء الاستخدام الليلي أو داخل الورش والطاولات العملية. وتمنح هذه الإضاءة توزيعًا جيدًا للضوء حول منطقة الرؤية، مما يسهل متابعة التفاصيل الصغيرة بشكل أوضح وأكثر راحة.

يأتي المنتج بتصميم يدوي مريح يسهل الإمساك به أثناء الاستخدام لفترات مختلفة، كما أن جسمه خفيف نسبيًا وعملي في الحمل والتخزين. ويمكن الاحتفاظ به بسهولة داخل درج المكتب أو صندوق العدة أو بالقرب من مكان العمل لاستخدامه عند الحاجة. وهذا يجعله مناسبًا للطلاب، والفنيين، والهواة، وكبار السن، وكل من يحتاج إلى أداة بسيطة وعملية لتحسين الرؤية القريبة.

بفضل الجمع بين التكبير والإضاءة في أداة واحدة، يعتبر هذا المنتج خيارًا عمليًا لعدد كبير من الاستخدامات اليومية والفنية، سواء لقراءة النصوص الصغيرة أو لفحص القطع الدقيقة أو للأعمال اليدوية التي تتطلب رؤية أوضح.

blocks.text: The HC-SR505 Mini PIR Motion Sensing Module uses the infrared radiation produced by body heat to detect motion at up to a distance of 10 feet.
Key Features of HC-SR505 Mini Motion Sensing Module
Detects body heat at distance of up to 10 feet

PIR (Passive Infrared) Motion Sensors are used to detect motion. They work by detecting the changes in infrared radiation that come from body heat. The sensor has two windows that have different fields of view. Since infrared comes from many different sources, it is differences in infrared between what the two sensor windows detect within a short period of time that is determined to be motion.
This sensor is similar to the HC-SR501, but this is a smaller package with fixed default operation and a bit easier to use whereas the HC-SR501 has a number of options that can be set.

The sensor has a range of 3-4 meters (9-12 feet). When triggered, the sensor output goes HIGH for approximately 6-12 seconds then returns LOW. If motion continues within the sensor range, the module will continue to retrigger and keep the output HIGH until the motion stops for at least 6-12 seconds. The length of the time delay varies between sensors, but is fairly consistent for a given sensor. The sensor has a white plastic dome over it. This dome is used to increase the field of view and to help provide some protection to the sensor. The field of view is approximately 100 degrees.

A common use for the sensor is to detect when a person or animal moves in or out of the sensor range and then take some action such as turning lights on/off, enabling a fan, enabling a Halloween prop or perhaps taking a picture.

Basic operation is simple. Just apply 5V and ground to the module. The sensor output is a logic HIGH when motion is detected and LOW when it is idle. This output can be connected to a uC or it can be connected directly to a relay module that can handle a logic level input in some cases if you just want to turn something on/off based on motion.

When the sensor is first powered on, it learns the ambient IR signature of its environment. Basically it is calibrating itself to its environment so that it can determine what constitutes motion. This takes around 15 seconds.

During that calibration time, false triggers are likely to occur so any triggers during this time should be ignored. It is important that there is not a lot of motion in the sensors view when it is going through its self-calibration as that can interfere with the calibration process.

The module has a very low power draw of about 70uA even when active. Because of the low power requirements, it can be powered off a digital output pin from a microcontroller if desired. If that is done, keep in mind the 15 second startup time.
There is a 3-pin header on the assembly.

The E13003 is a bipolar junction transistor (BJT) of the NPN type, functioning as a fundamental solid-state switch and amplifier for electronic circuits. Its core operation relies on using a small current applied to its base terminal to control a much larger current flow between its collector and emitter. Housed in a robust TO-126 package, this transistor is designed to handle substantial power levels, with the package itself acting as a crucial interface for dissipating generated heat to an external heatsink, thereby ensuring stable and reliable operation under load.

This device is engineered for medium-to-high voltage applications, characterized by a collector-to-emitter voltage rating of 400 volts. This high voltage capability makes it suitable for circuits operating directly from rectified mains electricity. It can support a continuous collector current of up to 1.5 amperes, allowing it to drive significant loads. The transition frequency of 4MHz indicates its operational speed limit, defining it as a component best suited for power switching and low-frequency amplification rather than for high-speed radio frequency applications.

In practice, the E13003 is often deployed in linear power supplies and offline switching power supplies, where it is repeatedly cycled between its fully on (saturation) and fully off (cut-off) states. Its ability to withstand high voltages and currents makes it a common choice for the power regulation and conversion stages of various electronic equipment. When in use, careful attention must be paid to its base drive current and operating temperature to ensure it remains within its safe operating area, preventing thermal runaway and ensuring long-term durability.

blocks.text: These infrared emitting LEDs operate at 940nm and used for creating IR remote control or IR obstacle and intrusion sensors.
KEY FEATURES OF IR EMITTER LED
Infrared is the light spectrum up around 940 nm that is commonly used for IR remotes and is outside the visible spectrum for the human eye.

These devices are very useful for adding IR capability to a project including everything from making a custom IR remote for your TV to creating a custom serial IR communication link for a robot project or to make an intrusion detector if the IR signal is blocked.
If you need a receiver for use with the transmitter, you may also want to pick up our IR phototransistor or IR receiver module.

The LED is easy to use and similar to normal LEDs in operation. Connect the cathode lead to ground and drive the anode lead with a logic high to turn on the LED. As with any LED, a current limiting series resistor is needed to protect the LED and/or the device being used to drive it.

The LED has a forward voltage drop of 1.2 to 1.4V. If driving it off a 5V MCU, a resistor value of 120 ohms will limit the current to a level of about 30mA. This is typically safe when pulsing the LED as is typically done in most applications. If driving the LED constantly on with an MCU, keeping the current down under 20mA is generally required depending on the MCU being used.

Since IR light is not visible to the human eye, it will appear that the LED is doing nothing so you will need something that is sensitive to IR light to detect that the LED is actually operating. For a quick check, the camera on a cell phone is more sensitive to IR light, so if you view the LED through your phone camera, you should be able to see it operating. You can of course also use something like our IR Receiver module for detecting the IR as well.

For remote control applications, the IR is typically pulsed at a modulated rate of 38kHz to created coded messages. Different manufacturers have different transmission protocols for these coded messages. There is a library that can be used with Arduino called IR Remote if you are looking to create a remote control application.

The IR emitter can also be used as part of an emitter / detector pair where an object is detected if it breaks the beam between the two. In this case, the IR emitter is usually driven on all the time rather than being pulsed.

The circuit below is an easy way to setup a simple IR emitter / IR phototransistor pair to experiment with basic operation. When the IR phototransistor detects IR from the IR LED, it will turn on and light the IR Detected LED. The brightness of the LED will depend on the strength of the IR that is detected. Note: If the IR Detected LED only glows slightly, make sure that the IR Phototransistor leads are not reversed.

blocks.text: The SP485E is a half-duplex differential transceiver designed to interface digital logic with balanced RS-485 and RS-422 serial buses. It combines a differential line driver and receiver in one integrated circuit, allowing the same bus pair to be used for transmitting and receiving at different times. The device belongs to the enhanced version of the SP485 family and is designed around a low-power BiCMOS process.

Internally, the driver accepts logic data at the DI input and converts it into complementary differential signals on the A and B lines. The receiver monitors the voltage difference between these bus lines and reproduces the received logic state at RO. Separate DE and RE control inputs determine whether the driver and receiver are active or placed in a high-impedance state, providing controlled access to the communication bus.

The MOC3041 is a Zero-Crossing TRIAC driven Optocoupler. Meaning it has a Infra-red Light Emitting Diode (LED) inside it coupled with a TRIAC. When the LED is triggered the TRIAC is also turned on.

blocks.v: Anode (A) · Anode pin of the IR LED. Connected to logic input
Cathode (C) · Cathode pin of the IR LED
NC · No Connection – Cannot be used
Triac Main Terminal 1 · One end of the Triac which is present inside the IC
NC · No Connection – Cannot be used
Triac Main Terminal 2 · Other end of the Triac which is present inside the IC

blocks.text: An opto-isolator like MOC3041 is normally used to control another external switching device like a TRIAC, MOSFET or SCR which in turn will control an AC or DC load. The TRIAC present inside the MOC3041 can provide upto 1A peak current which is high enough to trigger an external switch. The TRIAC by itself should not be used to switch loads without an external switch.

Since the MOC3041 has built-in Zero crossing detector it is mostly used in switching AC loads. A Zero cross detector will monitor for the 0V in output sine wave and turn on the internal TRIAC only during 0V. This way the LOAD will not be subjected to peak voltage when switching.

MOC3041 is commonly used in AC motor speed control, Light dimmers or other home automation application where AC load is involed. A typical application circuit diagram to control an ACload using a Microcontroller is shown below

The internal IR LED is connected between pin 1 and pin 2. The voltage source Vcc should be able to provide 15mA through resistor Rin to the Anode pin of the LED. The NAND gate connects the Cathode pin of the LED to ground based on a PWM signal from the microcontroller. So one input pin of NAND gate will be connected to ground while the other is connected to the PWM signal.

Based on the PWM signal the LED will be turned on at particular interval for which the internal TRIAC will also be turned on. When the internal TRIAC is turned on it switches the external TRIAC which in turn controls the AC load. The 39 ohms Resistor and the 0.01uF capacitors forma an optional Snubber circuit. Thus based on the duty cycle of the PWM the output voltage will also vary which enables us the control the speed of intensity of the load.

blocks.text: Water Level Detection Sensor Module — Analog Output, 3–5V, 40×16 mm Detection Area

This water level detection sensor is a low‑cost, resistive probe board that outputs an analog voltage proportional to the wet length of its exposed traces. It’s ideal for quick experiments with Arduino/ESP32/Raspberry Pi to detect presence, drops, leaks, or approximate level within a short range. The sensing area is approximately 40 × 16 mm, and the module operates from 3–5 V, drawing less than 20 mA.

Unlike float switches or ultrasonic sensors, this board is designed for near‑surface/short‑range detection. For continuous immersion or corrosive liquids, consider a sealed or non‑contact solution; this board is best for learning, prototyping, and indicative sensing.

Resistive principle: Water bridging across adjacent exposed traces forms a resistance ladder. The board converts this to a proportional output voltage.
Calibration: Map the dry reading and the fully‑wet reading to your 0–100% scale. Use moving average or median filter to reduce noise.
Corrosion & lifespan: The exposed copper can corrode with long‑term exposure, electrolytic action, or contaminated water. For reliability:
Use distilled water for tests where possible.
Power‑gate the sensor and sample intermittently (e.g., MOSFET on +V) to reduce electrolysis.
Consider anti‑corrosion or float/ultrasonic level sensors for permanent installations.
Not a linear level gauge: Output is monotonic but not perfectly linear; treat readings as indicative.
EMI/ESD: Keep leads short; add a 100 nF ceramic decoupling near +V.

Example thresholding: For leak detection, trigger alarm if averaged reading rises above a dry baseline + margin. For simple tank “near full” indication, mount the board vertically and set a threshold near the desired waterline.

blocks.text: Wheel 120×60mm Off-Road Robot Wheel Silver Rim – Single Wheel

The 120×60mm Off-Road Robot Wheel Silver Rim – Single Wheel is a large robotic drive wheel designed for projects that need stronger grip, a wider contact surface, and a more stable rolling profile than standard small robot wheels. This version is supplied as one wheel only, and it is suitable for smart cars, robotic platforms, educational vehicles, and custom motion systems that require a large off-road style wheel.

With an outer diameter of 120mm and a width of 60mm, this wheel provides a broad footprint that helps improve stability and traction during movement. The wide tire profile makes it especially useful in robot platforms that operate on mixed indoor and light outdoor surfaces, or in applications where better grip is needed during acceleration, turning, or load carrying.

The outer tire is made of flexible black rubber, which helps the wheel maintain good surface contact and reduces slipping. The tread pattern is designed for off-road style use, giving the wheel a more aggressive grip profile than ordinary smooth robot wheels. This makes it a strong option for DIY robotic cars, outdoor smart vehicles, and experimental mobile platforms.

The rim features a silver finish, giving the wheel a clean and attractive look while maintaining a lightweight structure suitable for robotics use. The wheel is designed for use with compatible mounting systems and motor shaft arrangements, but in this product version it is sold as wheel only without coupler.

This wheel is a practical choice for builders who already have their own adapter or coupling solution and only need the wheel itself. It can be used in larger robot chassis, motorized platforms, and custom RC-style builds where a large-diameter wheel is needed for better clearance and stronger mechanical presence.
Suitable For: Robot cars, smart vehicles, mobile robotic platforms
عجلة روبوت أوف رود 120×60 مم جنط فضي – قطعة واحدة

عجلة روبوت أوف رود 120×60 مم جنط فضي – قطعة واحدة هي عجلة كبيرة مخصصة للمشروعات التي تحتاج مقاس أكبر من العجلات التقليدية، سواء لتحسين الثبات أو زيادة التماسك أو إعطاء العربة قدرة أفضل على الحركة فوق الأسطح المختلفة. هذا المنتج يأتي في صورة عجلة واحدة فقط، وبدون كابلر، لذلك هو مناسب لمن لديه بالفعل طريقة التثبيت أو نظام الربط الخاص به.

العجلة بقطر 120 مم وعرض 60 مم، وده يعطيها حجمًا واضحًا وقاعدة تماس كبيرة مع الأرض. النتيجة العملية لذلك هي حركة أكثر ثباتًا، وتحكم أفضل أثناء اللف، وقدرة أعلى على التعامل مع أرضيات متنوعة مقارنة بالعجلات الصغيرة. هذا المقاس مناسب جدًا للعربات الروبوتية الأكبر نسبيًا أو المنصات التي تحتاج شكل قوي وأداء عملي في نفس الوقت.

الجزء الخارجي مصنوع من كاوتش أسود مرن، وده يساعد على تحسين الاحتكاك مع الأرض وتقليل الانزلاق أثناء الحركة أو التسارع أو الدوران. كما أن شكل النقشة الخارجية يعطي الطابع الأوف رود، وبالتالي تكون العجلة مناسبة أكثر للمشروعات التي تحتاج قبضة أفضل من العجلات الملساء العادية.

أما قلب العجلة فيأتي بلون فضي، وهو يعطي شكلًا أنيقًا ومميزًا، مع جسم مناسب للاستخدام في تطبيقات الروبوت والعربات الذكية. وبما أن المنتج هنا بدون كابلر، فهو مناسب أكثر للمستخدم الذي يريد شراء العجلة فقط واستخدامها مع وصلة أو محور أو كابلر موجود عنده بالفعل.

هذه العجلة مناسبة لمشروعات الروبوت، والعربات التعليمية، والمنصات المتحركة، والتطبيقات التي تحتاج عجلة كبيرة تتحمل الحركة وتعطي توازنًا أفضل. ولو المشروع عندك يحتاج عجلة كبيرة بإطار عريض وشكل أوف رود، فهذه النسخة تعتبر اختيار عملي جدًا.

The KCD4 Rocker Switch is a versatile and durable switch designed for use in a wide range of electrical and electronic applications. It supports a high current rating of 16A at 250V AC, making it suitable for both residential and industrial environments where robust power control is required.

This switch combines momentary and self-locking (latching) functions, offering flexible control depending on how it’s wired. The momentary function allows the switch to return to its original position after being pressed—ideal for temporary actions like triggering a motor or a reset command. On the other hand, the self-locking function lets the switch stay in its ON or OFF position until it is manually changed, perfect for maintaining continuous operation of lights, fans, or other equipment.

The 6-pin configuration allows for dual-pole or multi-function connections, making it adaptable to various circuit requirements. The switch is typically mounted on control panels or equipment housings, and its snap-in panel mount design ensures easy and secure installation.

Made with high-quality plastic and metal contacts, the KCD4 switch offers excellent durability and long life under frequent operation. Its rocker-style design ensures smooth and reliable actuation, with clear ON/OFF markings for user-friendly operation.

Whether you’re working on a home appliance, power tool, or custom electronic project, the KCD4 rocker switch provides a dependable, high-capacity switching solution. Its ability to handle high loads, along with the choice between momentary and latching functions, makes it ideal for a variety of applications, including HVAC systems, industrial machines, automotive electronics, and more.

74HC192-74192 (Decade Counter) is a high-quality electronic component designed for Arduino, prototyping, and educational electronics.
The 74192 is a Presettable Synchronous 4-Bit Up/Down Decade Counter.

Presetting the counter to the number on the preset data inputs (Input A – Input D) is accomplished by a LOW asynchronous parallel load input (Load). The counter is incremented on the low-to-high transition of the UP input (and a high level on the Clock- DOWN) and decremented on the low to high transition of the DOWN input (and a high level on the UP input). A high level on the CLR input overrides any other input to clear the counter to its zero state. The Terminal Count up (CO) goes low half a clock period before the zero count is reached and returns to a high level at the zero count.

The Terminal Count Down (BO) in the count down mode likewise goes low half a clock period before the maximum count (9 in the 74192) and returns to high at the maximum count. Cascading is effected by connecting the CO [carry] and BO [borrow] outputs of a less significant counter to the Clock-Up [UP] and Clock-Down [DOWN] inputs, respectively, of the next most significant counter.

Running from 12V rather than a lower 5V USB-style supply gives this module more headroom to drive larger, more demanding speakers than a typical 5V amplifier board can comfortably handle, making it a popular choice for DIY Bluetooth speaker builds – commonly paired with a separate Bluetooth audio receiver module to provide the wireless input – small PA/announcement speaker projects, and general 12V-powered audio amplification builds.

This reliable mechanism ensures effective water management by preventing issues like overflow, dry running of pumps, or inefficient use of water resources.

3duino-8832.summary: The IR Infrared Obstacle Avoidance Sensor is a compact reflective proximity module for detecting nearby objects without physical contact. It operates from 3.3V to 5V, provides an active-low digital output, and features an adjustable detection range of approximately 2–30cm. Ideal for Arduino robots, smart cars, object counters, and automatic control projects.

blocks.text: The IR Infrared Obstacle Avoidance Sensor is a compact electronic module designed to detect nearby objects using reflected infrared light. It combines an infrared transmitting LED, an infrared receiver, an LM393 comparator circuit, and an adjustable sensitivity control on a small circuit board.

When an object enters the detection area, infrared light emitted by the transmitter reflects from the object and returns to the receiver. The onboard comparator processes this reflected signal and changes the state of the digital output. Therefore, the module can be connected directly to an Arduino, ESP32, ESP8266, STM32, Raspberry Pi GPIO, or another digital control circuit.

The IR Infrared Obstacle Avoidance Sensor provides an adjustable detection range of approximately 2cm to 30cm. The onboard potentiometer allows the user to change the switching threshold according to the required application.

However, this range is approximate rather than guaranteed. White and reflective objects can usually be detected from a greater distance than dark, transparent, or highly absorbent surfaces. Furthermore, strong sunlight and other infrared light sources can affect the reading.

The module provides a digital output rather than an analog distance measurement. When no obstacle is detected, the OUT pin is normally HIGH. When an object is detected within the adjusted range, the output changes to LOW.

As a result, the module tells the controller whether an obstacle is present, but it does not provide the exact distance to that obstacle. For accurate numerical distance measurement, an ultrasonic or time-of-flight distance sensor should be used instead.

After connecting the sensor, place the target object at the required detection distance. Slowly rotate the onboard potentiometer until the detection LED changes state. Move the object closer and farther several times to verify reliable switching.

Calibration should be performed using an object similar in color and material to the object used in the final application. Additionally, test the module under the actual lighting conditions because sunlight and reflective surfaces can affect infrared performance.
This sensor does not measure exact distance. It only provides an on/off detection signal according to the adjusted threshold.

Detection performance varies according to the object’s color, shape, angle, material, and reflectivity. Dark or transparent objects may require a shorter detection distance. Therefore, the sensor should be calibrated after final installation.

The module is also different from a PIR motion sensor. A PIR sensor detects changes in infrared radiation from warm objects such as people, while this module actively emits infrared light and detects its reflection from nearby surfaces.
